overview.description: Queen's Slipper 500 is the definitive Australian version of the card game 500, played using specialized decks produced by the iconic Queen's Slipper brand. While standard 500 exists, the Australian variant is unique for its use of 11s, 12s, and 13s, allowing for 4, 5, or even 6-player games with expanded decks. It is a trick-taking game that evolved from Euchre, featuring a complex bidding system, the 'MisÃ¨re' (no-trick) contract, and the inclusion of a Joker as the ultimate trump card.

history.origins: Originally created in the US in 1904 by the US Playing Card Co. It spread to Australia where the 'Queen's Slipper' brand popularized a variant with expanded suit counts and the MisÃ¨re bid.
timeline: 1904: USPC Co copyrights the original 500 rules.
1920s: Gathers immense popularity in Australia, becoming the national social game.
1960s: Queen's Slipper brand (Lenz) standardizes the '500's Deck' with 11s, 12s, and 13s.
Present: Remains a core cultural institution in Australian community centers, schools, and homes.
history.evolution: The game moved from a 10-trick structure to include high-stakes 'Kitty' swaps and the famous 'Double MisÃ¨re' variants.
history.cultural: Commonly played as a 'Pub Game' and in formal 500 clubs across Melbourne and regional Victoria.

setup.deck: 43 cards for a 4-handed game: 4s to Aces, plus the Joker and the 11s/12s of specific suits (depends on house rules).
setup.dealing: 3 cards, 1 to kitty, 4 cards, 1 to kitty, 3 cards, 1 to kitty (Total: 10 cards each, 3 in kitty).

rules.objective: Be the first team to reach 500 points or force opponents to -500 points.
rules.gameplay: Partners sit opposite. Deal 10 each and 3 to kitty. Bid from six tricks in a suit or No Trumps, or Misere (lose every trick) or Open Misere. Highest bidder takes kitty, discards three, and leads. Follow suit; trick to highest trump or highest of led suit. Joker is highest trump; Right and Left Bower next. First team to 500 wins; minus 500 loses.
keyRules: Bidding order: Spades lowest, Clubs, Diamonds, Hearts, No Trumps. Misere only after someone bid seven. Contractor picks up kitty and discards three. Must follow suit. Trick winner leads next. Opponents score 10 per trick taken when contractors make contract.

strategy.basic: Count your Bowers! The Jack of the trump suit (Right) and its same-colored brother (Left) are more powerful than the Ace. If you hold the Joker and both Bowers, you possess the 'The Nuts'â€”you can lead with them to clear all other trumps from the table. Don't bid heavily if you only have high Aces; you can easily be blocked by the Jacks.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Kitty' Discard: After you win the bid and take the Kitty, you must discard three cards. Don't just discard your lowest cards. If you have only one card of a specific suit (a 'Singleton'), discard it! This allows you to trump that suit the first time it is led, gaining a trick you would have otherwise lost.
strategy.advanced: MisÃ¨re Defense: If an opponent bids MisÃ¨re, your team must work together to 'Force' them to win a trick. Lead suits where you have many low cards. If you see the MisÃ¨re player stalling on a suit (e.g., they play a 7 when you lead a 4), they are afraid of that suit. Lead it again! Defense against MisÃ¨re is about 'Hand-Squeezing' the bidder until they have no choice but to take a trick.
tips: A 'Seven Spades' bid is the lowest possible. It's often used just to see of your partner has anything.
The Joker is worth 0 in No Trump if led, but is still the highest cardâ€”remember the No Trump special rules.

list.name: Joker in No Trumps
list.description: Some play that in No Trumps the joker cannot be nominated in advance as belonging to a suit; or that the joker cannot be played on a lead of a suit on which you have previously reneged.
list.emptyOverridesReason: House-rule variant; engine overrides not yet mapped for joker nomination rules.

list.name: Bidding process
list.description: Some allow bidding after pass (auction continues until three passes in succession). Some allow the contractor to raise the final bid after everyone has passed.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Auction timing variant; overrides for bid-after-pass need further source lookup.

list.name: Misere ranking and scoring
list.description: House rules vary: Misere allowed only after a seven bid; Open Misere ranking between 9 No Trumps and 10 Spades or as highest; alternative scores (e.g. Misere 150, Open Misere 250, misere without pickup 350).
list.emptyOverridesReason: Scoring and ranking vary by house; overrides for scores and ranking not yet defined.

difficulty.easy: Doesn't understand Bower rankings; wastes Joker early; poor MisÃ¨re defense.
difficulty.medium: Reasonable bidding; manages Kitty swaps; basic partnership signaling.
difficulty.hard: Expert 'Bower-Tracker'; perfectly simulates MisÃ¨re pitfalls; manipulates the Kitty to create Voids.

phases.label: Bidding
phases.notes: Bidding starts left of dealer. Minimum six tricks; suit or No Trumps or Misere or Open Misere. Pass means cannot bid again. Highest bid wins.

phases.label: Kitty pickup
phases.notes: Contractor picks up three kitty cards and discards three face down.

phases.label: Play
phases.notes: Contractor leads. Follow suit if able. Trick won by highest trump or highest of led suit. Winner leads next.

play_card.description: Play one card to the current trick. Must follow suit if able. Trick won by highest trump, or if no trump by highest card of led suit. Winner of trick leads to next.
play_card.constraints: Legal when it is your turn in the play phase. Must follow suit if you have a card of the suit led.

pass.description: Decline to bid; pass means you cannot bid again in that auction.
pass.constraints: Legal during bidding when it is your turn to speak.

bid.description: Bid a number of tricks (6–10) and a trump suit, or No Trumps, or Misere, or Open Misere. Each bid must be higher than the previous. Order: Spades lowest, then Clubs, Diamonds, Hearts, No Trumps. Misere only after someone bid seven; Open Misere can be bid over any.
bid.constraints: Legal during bidding when it is your turn; must be higher than current bid. Once passed you cannot bid again.

trumpConfig.trumpSuitRanking: Joker highest, then Jack of trump (Right Bower), Jack of same colour (Left Bower), then A K Q 10 9 8 7 6 5 or 4. Same-colour suit has no Jack.
trumpConfig.overtakingRule: Trump beats non-trump; highest trump wins; no trump then highest of led suit wins.

customActions.description: Deal 3 cards to each player, 1 to kitty, 4 to each, 1 to kitty, 3 to each, 1 to kitty. Total 10 per player, 3 in kitty.
customActions.constraints: Dealer only; at start of hand.

customActions.description: Pick up the three kitty cards (without showing opponents) and discard any three cards face down in their place.
customActions.constraints: Contractor only; immediately after winning the bid.

engine.handRankingSystem: Trick-taking; contract value from scoring table; Joker and Bowers rank above Ace in trump.
engine.deckDescription: For Australian four-handed 500 a 43-card pack is used: A K Q J 10 9 8 7 6 5 4 in the red suits, A K Q J 10 9 8 7 6 5 in the black suits, plus one Joker (the bird). Standard 52 plus Joker can be used; remove cards as needed for the 43-card layout. Queen's Slipper and other 500 decks may include 11s, 12s, 13s for five- or six-handed play.
engine.suitDescription: Four traditional French suits: Hearts (Cœur), Diamonds (Carreau), Clubs (Trèfle), and Spades (Pique), each represented with standard French card design and distinct color coding for quick suit recognition during trick-taking play.
engine.rankDescription: Standard thirteen ranks per suit: Ace, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, Jack, Queen, and King, where certain ranks (particularly Queens and Sixes) carry special scoring value in this 500-point trick-taking game.
engine.dealPattern: 3 each, 1 kitty, 4 each, 1 kitty, 3 each, 1 kitty
